rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience to God means carrying out commands and stopping at prohibitions with awareness of His greatness, continually and anew.
rows.anchor: في امتثال أوامره والوقوف عند زواجره مستحضرا عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience to the Messenger extends to everything he wills, because the office of messengership requires it.
rows.anchor: أي ي كل ما أراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being with the favored means belonging to their company and reaching them easily to visit or see them, not necessarily sharing their rank when one's deeds are lesser.
rows.anchor: أي معدود من حزبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets are informed by God of subtle wisdom and convey refined words, with purified character and lofty stature.
rows.anchor: أي الذين أنبأهم الله بدقائق الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truthful are first to affirm what came from God and truthful in speech and action, becoming examples for those after them.
rows.anchor: أي الذين صدقوا أول الناس ما أتاهم عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses remain present to the sacred realm, testify to God's religion and against its opposite by proof or sword, and are then killed in God's path.
rows.anchor: أي الذين لم يغيبوا أصلا عن حضرات القدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous have no corruption in outward or inward life through God's power.
rows.anchor: الذي لا يعرتيهم في ظاهر ولا باطن بحول الله فساد أصلا

rows.speaker: الشيخ رسلان
rows.claim: Righteousness is not complete while any remnant of attachment to other than God remains within a person.
rows.anchor: ما صلحت ما دامت فيك بقية لسواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All four qualities may gather in one person, though they need not do so.
rows.anchor: وقد تجتمع الصفات الأربع في شخص وقد لا تجتمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr is the community's most deserving truthful one even if Ali and Zayd accepted Islam before him.
rows.anchor: وأبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه أحق الأمة بالصديقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr's age and independence from following the Prophet before Islam made him an exemplar whose conversion led many others to Islam and multiplied his reward.
rows.anchor: لكبره وكونه لم يكن قبل الإسلام تابعا للنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr's defense of the Prophet and other actions showed his truthfulness and helped place him immediately after prophethood.
rows.anchor: وكان فيه حين إسلامه قوة الجهاد في الله سبحانه وتعالى بالمدافعة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God honored this community by making Abu Bakr their successor after the Prophet and burying him beside the Prophet, removing an intermediary between their ranks.
rows.anchor: ولرفع الواسطة بينهما وفق الله سبحانه وتعالى هذه الأمة التي اختارها بتولية الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه بعد نبيهم صلى الله عليه وسلم ودفنه إلى جانبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the portrayal of the Messenger and the complete, lucid Book, then divides those warned by the surah.
rows.anchor: أخذ يقسم المنذرين فقال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in God recognizes that no one shares with Him in essence, attributes, acts, rulings, or names, as decisive proof makes clear.
rows.anchor: لا أمر لأحد معه في ذاته وصفاته وأفعاله وأحكامه وأسمائه بما دل عليه قاطع البرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Holding fast to God means making Him the bond that keeps believers steady in obligations and prevents a return from guidance to error.
rows.anchor: أي جعلوه عصاما لهم في الفرائض التي هي من أعظم مقاصد هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for holding fast has an intensive, effortful form because people tend toward neglect, which produces misguidance.
rows.anchor: وصيغة الافتعال تدل على الاجتهاد في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future promise is certain; the future particle may also urge perseverance in action because God's reward is precious.
rows.anchor: أي بوعد لا خلف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised mercy is a great reward granted by grace, not something believers deserve through their own merit.
rows.anchor: أي ثواب عظيم هو برحمته لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added favor is a great increase that believers know they did not cause or earn.
rows.anchor: أي عظيم يعلمون أنه زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides them in this life and the next to a clear, straight path that protects them inwardly and outwardly and enables them to follow obligations and other guidance.
rows.anchor: أي في الدنيا والآخرة { إليه صراطا } أي عظيما واضحا جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division marker introduces one side of the two groups mentioned in the previous verse; their adherence to God's rulings whatever their desires exposes hypocrites and those who accept only part of revelation.
rows.anchor: بأما المقتضية للتقسيم لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition to inheritance is seamless, without a conjunction, and criticizes repeated questions about women and children after a sufficient answer, presenting the clearest path.
rows.anchor: وترك القسم الآخر وهو قسم المستنكفين والمستكبرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalala is a person without either a child or a parent.
rows.anchor: وهو من لا ولد له

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bara reports that the last surah revealed was Bara'a and the last verse revealed was the kalala ruling in 4:176.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري في التفسير عن البراء رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr defined kalala as what remains besides the father.
rows.anchor: اختلف أبو بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما في الكلالة

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar defined kalala as what remains besides both parent and child, then said he was ashamed before God to oppose Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر : ما عدا الوالد والولد

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi is the authority through whom al-Asbahani reports the disagreement between Abu Bakr and Umar about kalala.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصبهاني عن الشعبي : اختلف أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deceased has no child, male or female and however distant, and no parent; if either exists, the case is not kalala, as the Sunna clarifies.
rows.anchor: أي وإن سفل سواء كان ذكرا أو أنثى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's rule is to give prescribed shares first and then the remainder to the closest male agnate; this also establishes that a father takes precedence over a brother.
rows.anchor: ألحقوا الفرائض بأهلها فما بقي فلأولى عصبة ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single sister may be full or paternal; a uterine sister is excluded because her brother does not make her an agnatic heir.
rows.anchor: أي واحدة من أب شقيقة كانت أو لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the sister dies without a child, her brother inherits her estate; if she leaves a daughter, he shares with her and does not take the whole estate.
rows.anchor: أي إن ماتت هي وبقي هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two paternal or full sisters receive two-thirds; if one is full and the other paternal, the full sister gets one-half and the paternal sister one-sixth to complete two-thirds.
rows.anchor: فإن كانت شقيقتين كان لكم منهما ثلث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among mixed male and female siblings, each male receives the share of two females; the concise passage completes the inheritance cases intended here.
rows.anchor: أي مختلطين { رجالا وسناء فللذكر } أي منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The placement warns that refusing inheritance to women and minors is arrogance against worship; rejecting any one divine ruling is real disbelief, even if other rulings are accepted.
rows.anchor: من أبى توريث النساء والصغار الذي تكرر الاستفتاء عنه فقد استنكف عن عبادته واستكبر وإن آمن بجميع ما عداه من الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended enemies are knowledgeable, envious People of the Book who know these rulings are true and want Muslims misled into sharing their misery after changing God's rulings.
rows.anchor: شياطين أهل الكتاب العارفين بصحة هذه الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wants to clarify and guide people along the ways of those before them, while followers of desire want believers to deviate greatly.
rows.anchor: يريد الله ليبين لكم ويهديكم سنن الذين من قبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book who received scripture buy misguidance and want believers to leave the path, explaining their role in the inheritance dispute.
rows.anchor: ألم تر إلى الذين أوتوا نصيبا من الكتاب يشترون الضلالة ويريدون أن تضلوا السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending says God makes the ruling clear from complete knowledge and does not leave its explanation to anyone else, so people will not stray.
rows.anchor: أي الذي أحاط بكل شيء قدرة وعلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has clarified what benefits people in life and death, this world and the next, leaving them on a clear path in daylight from which only the doomed stray.
rows.anchor: فقد بين لكم بعلمه ما يصلحكم بيانه محيا ومماتا دنيا وأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inheritance passage is delayed so resistant rulings can be presented gradually and gently, and to emphasize inheritance throughout the surah.
rows.anchor: تأخير هذه الآية إلى هنا لما تقدم من أن تفريق القول فيما تأباه النفوس وإلقاءه شيئا فشيئا باللطف والتدريج أدعى لقبوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its placement warns against hypocrites and People of the Book who implant doubts, and against accepting some rulings while rejecting others, since religion is indivisible and rejecting any part rejects all.
rows.anchor: والترهيب من أن يكونوا مثلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's opening treats humanity as one community; its end likewise gives women and men inheritance through kinship, though their shares differ, and warns that rejecting any divine ruling brings punishment without a helper.
rows.anchor: لأن أولها مشير إلى أن الناس كلهم كشيء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The end's comprehensive knowledge corresponds to the opening's complete power, because perfect knowledge entails encompassing power.
rows.anchor: وما أشد مناسبة ختامها بإحاطة العلم لما دل عليه أولها من تمام القدرة

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The two attributes of knowledge and power establish lordship, divinity, majesty, and might, requiring servants to obey commands and prohibitions and submit to all duties.
rows.anchor: وهذان الوصفان هما اللذان بهما ثبتت الربوية والإلهية والجلال والعزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He closes by turning to the phrase that ends the surah first verse, as a further link between its ending and opening.
rows.anchor: ولختام أول آية فيها بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing reminder that God knows every state and nothing escapes Him calls for heightened vigilance, and the surah's ending is especially apt to the opening of al-Ma'ida.
rows.anchor: فليشتد حذركم منه ومراقبتكم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After an ambiguous exemption, the passage explains what remains lawful and starts with prohibitions lasting until their proper place; its opening also broadly bars violation of sacred signs, especially those marked by ihram.
rows.anchor: ولما استثنى بعض ما أحل على سبيل الإبهام شرع في بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is repeated to honor and rouse the believers and remind them of the commitments they accepted on entering the religion willingly.
rows.anchor: مكررا لندائهم تنويها بشأنهم وتنبيها لعزائمهم وتذكيرا لهم بما ألزموه أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs mean the rites of pilgrimage or the limits of religion generally; pilgrimage rites are especially included, and hunting is the foremost case.
rows.anchor: أو حدوده في جميع الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular sacred month can refer to all sacred months, whose sanctity is equal in both pre-Islamic and Islamic practice.
rows.anchor: أي فإن ذلك لم معاقدا على احترامه في الجاهلية والإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the sanctuary and sacred months, the passage protects offerings and especially garlanded offerings, using the collars as an emphatic way to prohibit harming their owners.
rows.anchor: ذكر ما يهدى للحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those heading to the Sacred House must also be left unharmed: the sanctuary protects rational visitors just as it protects the animals brought there.
rows.anchor: ولا تحلوا التعرض لناس قاصدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visitors seek bounty as reward from God without a claim of true entitlement; adding His pleasure matters because reward could otherwise accompany displeasure.
rows.anchor: لأن ثوابه لا يكون على وجه الاستحقاق الحقيقي أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to seeking God's favor clearly includes Muslims and may include unbelievers, whose pilgrimage could soften the heart and prepare it for Islam.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد به أيضا الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If unbelieving visitors are included, the ruling is abrogated.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فهي منسوخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once released from ihram after completing rites or being blocked, hunting becomes permitted; hunting during sacred months was already forbidden, and the month is named to honor it.
rows.anchor: أي من الإحرام بقضاء المناسك والإحصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not let hatred lead to transgression; a Muslim's enemy crossing bounds should make the Muslim hold more firmly to the limits of the law, whether the provocation was at Hudaybiyya or elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي يحملنكم { شنئان قوم }

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read the clause with the conditional particle, while the other readers' fatḥ reading gives the sense of because they barred you.
rows.anchor: هذا في قراءة ابن كثير وأبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provocation was their barring Muslims from the Sacred Mosque at Hudaybiyya or another occasion; the rule precedes the later ban on polytheists approaching it in 9:28.
rows.anchor: أي في عام الحديبية أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteousness is broad, wholesome lawful good, while God-consciousness is everything that prompts fear of God; if someone transgresses, believers should help restrain them, otherwise they should cooperate in increasing good.
rows.anchor: وهو ما اتسع وطاب من حلال الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not help with sin or aggression, including boundary-crossing, revenge, or retaliation; anger toward a friend or relative is justified only when it calls to righteousness and piety.
rows.anchor: ناهيا أن يغضب الإنسان لغضب أحد من صديق أو قريب إلا إذا كان الغضب له داعيا إلى بر وتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to be mindful points to piety as the motive for every good and every observance of God's limits.
rows.anchor: وكرر الأمر بالتقوى إشارة إلى أنها الحاملة على كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending stresses severe punishment because suppressing revenge, anger, and the urge for vindication is especially difficult.
rows.anchor: ولما كان كف النفس عن الانتقام وزجرها عن شفاء داء الغيظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because dogs had been ordered killed and game could die before ritual slaughter, people asked which dogs or dead game were permitted; the preceding context made this question natural.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أمر بقتل الكلاب

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi transmits from Abu Rafi that after the Prophet ordered dogs killed, people asked what was lawful from a species they had been ordered to kill, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روى الواحدي في أسباب النزول بسنده عن أبي رافع رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says al-Hakim also narrated this report in his Sahih.
rows.anchor: رواه الحاكم أبو عبد الله في صحيحه

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: In the fuller account, Gabriel would not enter a house containing an image or dog; Abu Rafi was ordered to kill the city's dogs, spared a guard dog out of pity, then killed it on the Prophet's order.
rows.anchor: جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاستأذن عليه

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: After the verse, the Prophet permitted keeping dogs with a useful purpose, prohibited useless ones, ordered harmful black or biting dogs killed, and spared harmless dogs.
rows.anchor: فلما نزلت أذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في اقتناء الكلاب التي ينتفع بها

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said b. Jubayr says the verse concerned Adi b. Hatim and Zayd b. al-Muhalhil, whom the Prophet renamed Zayd al-Khayr, after they asked about dogs and falcons catching game that sometimes died before slaughter.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : نزلت هذه الآية في عدي بن حاتم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The two hunters asked because their dogs and falcons caught cattle, donkeys, gazelles, and monitor lizards; some prey could be slaughtered in time, while other prey died first, although carrion was forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : نزلت هذه الآية في عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن المهلهل

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said b. Jubayr glosses the wholesome things as slaughtered animals and the hunting animals as catching dogs and predatory birds.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : نزلت هذه الآية في عدي بن حاتم وزيد بن المهلهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording answers about food generally, rather than asking what God made lawful for us, and covers keeping dogs, game, and other foods.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا إخبارا عن غائب قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wholesome foods are those sound natures regard as pure, with no prohibited impurity or disgust; this includes lawful slaughter, animals once forbidden as sa'iba, seafood, and other permitted non-food benefits.
rows.anchor: فلا خبث فيها بنوع تحريم ولا تقذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hunting animals are called jawāriḥ because they wound or cause slaughter, or because the root also means earning.
rows.anchor: أي التي من شأنها أن تجرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term jawāriḥ also means earners, as in 6:60; here it refers to hunting predators and birds, whose keeping and hunting are permitted when trained.
rows.anchor: وهو كواسب الصيد من السباع والطير

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i says a dog is trained when it responds to a hunting signal, stops when restrained and does not eat the catch, answers when called, and does not flee when approached; this must happen repeatedly.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي : والكلب لا يصير معلما إلا عند أمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No fixed count is specified for these trained behaviors because, absent a revealed text or consensus, the judgment returns to customary usage.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر حدا لأن الاسم إذا لم يكن معلوما من نص ولا إجماع وجب الرجوع فيه إلى العرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The training clause is phrased around dogs although it covers all hunting animals because dogs require more training; it implies strenuous, careful instruction.
rows.anchor: وبنى الحال من الكلاب وإن كان المراد العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators say the circumstantial clause means the trainer must be highly skilled and precise in the training.
rows.anchor: وفائدة هذه الحال أن يكون المعلم نحريرا في علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The further clause about teaching the animals can be another circumstantial phrase or a resumption, covering wild animals and birds and crediting God as the source of this knowledge.
rows.anchor: وأكد ذلك بحال أخرى أو استئناف فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches every seeker to learn from the most knowledgeable and expert specialists, even if the journey is arduous.
rows.anchor: فأفاد ذلك أن على كل طالب لشيء أن لا يأخذه إلا من أجل العلماء به وأشدهم دراية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only game held for the hunter by trained instruction is lawful, including prey that dies before slaughter; prey held through the animal's own instinct and appetite is not lawful.
rows.anchor: إمساكها { عليكم } أي على تعليمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's name is spoken when releasing the hunting animal or when slaughtering prey reached alive, in contrast with pre-Islamic practice.
rows.anchor: أي على ما أمسكن عند إرسال الجارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about naming God relates to the exception from the prohibition of carrion in 5:3 and explains the rule against hunting while in ihram.
rows.anchor: وقد صارت نسبة هذه الجملة . كما ترى . إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Training hunting animals is unusual despite its familiarity, and hunting with them is wondrous in its method; this leads to a warning about God's swift reckoning and exact knowledge of deserved reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تعليم الجوارح أمرا خارجا عن العادة في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must account for themselves and fear God concerning whether prey was properly slaughtered and whether the animal held it for them or for itself.
rows.anchor: أي حاسبوا أنفسكم واتقوا { الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only one overcome by awe of God attends to all the fine distinctions of hunting law, fearing Him in what is permitted and forbidden.
rows.anchor: لا يقف عندها إلا من غلبت عليه مهابة اله واستشعره خوفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is swift to reckon because He knows everything and can act at any time, able to recompense as He wills without one person or affair distracting Him from another.
rows.anchor: أي عالم بكل شيء وقادر عليه في كل وقت
